question: In PowerPoint 2016; where do you find the THEMES gallery?
option_b: Insert tab
option_c: DESIGN tab — the Themes group contains built-in theme thumbnails that change the look of the entire presentation

question: What is a THEME in PowerPoint?
option_b: A coordinated set of COLOURS; FONTS; and EFFECTS (background styles; graphic effects) that gives the entire presentation a consistent professional look

question: What THREE components make up a PowerPoint THEME?
option_b: COLOURS; FONTS; and EFFECTS — all three coordinate together when a theme is applied

question: What is the VARIANTS section on the Design tab used for?
option_b: Applying colour VARIATIONS of the current theme — alternative colour palettes while keeping the same fonts and layout

question: To CUSTOMISE THE COLOURS of a theme in PowerPoint?
option_b: Design tab → Variants group → click the dropdown arrow → Colors → Customise Colors (opens a dialog to change each of the 12 colour slots)

question: What does the BACKGROUND STYLES option on the Design tab allow you to do?
option_b: Change the BACKGROUND of slides (solid colours; gradient fills; textures; pictures) independently of the theme colours

question: In PowerPoint 2016; a TRANSITION is applied to?
option_b: The SLIDE ITSELF — it is the visual effect seen when moving from one slide to the NEXT during a slideshow
option_d: The entire presentation at once (cannot be changed per slide)

question: What TAB in PowerPoint contains all the TRANSITION effects?
option_b: Animations
option_c: TRANSITIONS tab — contains the Transition to This Slide gallery; Effect Options; Timing; and Advance Slide settings

question: What does the EFFECT OPTIONS button do for a transition?
option_b: Changes the DIRECTION or STYLE of the selected transition (e.g. Wipe can go From Left; From Right; From Top; From Bottom)

question: What does the DURATION setting in the Transitions tab control?
option_a: How long a slide is displayed
option_b: How many seconds the transition ANIMATION takes to complete (e.g. 0.5 seconds for a fast transition; 3 seconds for a slow fade)
option_c: The delay before the next slide starts

question: What does the 'APPLY TO ALL' button do in the Transitions tab?
option_b: Applies the currently selected transition (with all its settings — effect; duration; sound; advance) to EVERY slide in the presentation
option_c: Applies the transition only to selected slides
option_d: Applies the transition to the current slide only

question: In the Advance Slide section (Transitions tab); what does 'After: 00:03.00' mean?
option_a: The slide appears 3 seconds before being clicked
option_b: The transition takes 3 seconds
option_c: The slide automatically advances to the NEXT slide after 3 seconds; without needing a mouse click or key press
option_d: The slide is shown for 30 seconds

question: What is the SOUND option in the Transitions tab?
option_a: Adds background music to the whole presentation
option_b: Adds a SOUND EFFECT that plays during the transition animation (e.g. a whoosh; a click; a drum roll)

question: The TRANSITIONS gallery in PowerPoint 2016 is divided into three categories. What are they?
option_b: SUBTLE; EXCITING; and DYNAMIC CONTENT

question: What does the MORPH transition do in PowerPoint 2016?
option_b: SMOOTHLY ANIMATES objects that appear on two consecutive slides — moving; scaling; and transforming shared objects to create a seamless animated effect

question: What is an ANIMATION in PowerPoint?
option_b: A visual effect applied to an INDIVIDUAL OBJECT (text; image; shape; SmartArt) ON A SINGLE SLIDE — it appears; disappears; or moves without leaving the slide
option_c: A video inserted on a slide

question: What TAB in PowerPoint 2016 contains all ANIMATION effects?
option_b: Design
option_c: ANIMATIONS tab — the Animation gallery; Effect Options; Advanced Animation (Add Animation; Animation Pane; Trigger); and Timing

question: The Animation gallery is grouped into four categories. What are they?
option_b: ENTRANCE; EMPHASIS; EXIT; and MOTION PATHS

question: What is an ENTRANCE animation?
option_a: An animation that makes an object disappear
option_b: An animation that makes an object EXIT the slide
option_c: An animation that makes an object APPEAR on the slide during the presentation (the object is hidden until the animation plays)
option_d: An animation that highlights an object

question: What is an EMPHASIS animation?
option_a: An animation applied to video clips
option_b: An animation that makes an object APPEAR
option_c: An animation that makes an object DISAPPEAR
option_d: An animation applied to an object ALREADY VISIBLE on the slide — it draws attention to it (e.g. Pulse; Spin; Grow; Change Colour) without making it appear or disappear

question: What is an EXIT animation?
option_a: An animation that makes an object appear
option_b: An animation that makes an object LEAVE THE SLIDE during the presentation (the object disappears when the animation plays)
option_d: An animation that moves the object

question: What is a MOTION PATH animation?
option_a: An animation that makes an object fade
option_b: An animation that makes an object move ALONG A DEFINED PATH on the slide (e.g. Line; Arc; Circle; Custom freehand path)
option_c: An animation that changes the object's colour
option_d: An animation that makes the object spin

question: What is the ANIMATION PANE in PowerPoint?
option_a: The slide panel on the left
option_b: A panel that lists ALL animations on the current slide in order; with controls for reordering; timing; and editing each animation

question: What does the 'START: ON CLICK' setting mean for an animation?
option_a: The animation plays automatically when the slide appears
option_b: The animation plays when the PRESENTER CLICKS THE MOUSE (or presses a key) — it waits for user input
option_c: The animation plays on a timer
option_d: The animation plays when the object is hovered over

question: What does 'START: WITH PREVIOUS' mean for an animation?
option_a: The animation starts after a click
option_b: The animation starts automatically AT THE SAME TIME as the previous animation (they play simultaneously; no additional click needed)
option_c: The animation starts before the slide appears
option_d: The animation starts at a random time

question: What does 'START: AFTER PREVIOUS' mean for an animation?
option_a: The animation plays before the previous animation ends
option_b: The animation starts automatically AFTER THE PREVIOUS ANIMATION FINISHES playing (a short delay can be added)
option_c: The animation plays on click only
option_d: The animation reverses the previous animation

question: What does the DELAY setting do for an animation?
option_b: Adds a PAUSE (in seconds) BEFORE the animation starts playing — giving the audience time to read existing content first

question: What does DURATION control in the Animation Timing settings?
option_b: How long the animation's visual effect takes to complete — e.g. 0.5s for a quick Fly In; 2s for a slow Fade In
option_c: The delay before the animation starts
option_d: The number of times the animation repeats

question: What does REPEAT do in an animation's timing settings?
option_b: Makes the animation play MULTIPLE TIMES (e.g. 2; 3; Until Next Click; Until End of Slide)
option_c: Adds a delay before the animation

question: What is a TRIGGER animation in PowerPoint?
option_a: An animation that plays on slide entry
option_b: An animation that plays when a specific OBJECT ON THE SLIDE IS CLICKED — click that object to start its animation
option_c: An animation with a custom path

question: What does 'ADD ANIMATION' (Animations → Advanced Animation → Add Animation) allow you to do?
option_b: Add a SECOND (or more) animation to the same object — so one object can have multiple sequential animations (e.g. Fly In → Pulse → Fly Out)
option_c: Add an animation to all slides

question: What is the purpose of using the ANIMATION PAINTER (eyedropper icon near the Animation Pane)?
option_b: COPIES animation settings from one object and pastes them onto another object — one click to copy to one object; double-click to copy to multiple objects

question: To PREVIEW all animations on a slide without starting the full slideshow?
option_b: Press Escape
option_c: Click PREVIEW (Animations tab → Preview) or click PLAY ALL in the Animation Pane to see all animations play on the slide in Normal view

question: What does clicking the PLAY ALL button in the Animation Pane do?
option_b: Plays ALL animations on the current slide in sequence in Normal view — useful for checking the full animation sequence without entering Slide Show mode

question: In Book 5 Chapter 4; students apply a THEME to a presentation then customise it. What customisation is taught?
option_b: Changing only the theme's fonts by Design → Variants → Fonts → Customise Fonts (to set a specific heading and body font pair)

question: What is the 'TRIGGER' feature in PowerPoint animations most useful for?
option_b: Creating INTERACTIVE presentations where clicking a specific shape; button; or image on the slide starts a specific animation — turning the slide into an interactive element

question: A student wants FIVE bullets to FLY IN one at a time; each triggered by a separate click. How should she set the animation for the text box?
option_a: One Fly In animation with Start: After Previous
option_b: Select the text box → Animation Fly In → Effect Options → By 1st Level Paragraphs; set Start to 'On Click' — each bullet will fly in on a separate click
option_c: Animate each bullet separately using 5 text boxes
option_d: Use a transition for each bullet

question: What does the MORPH transition REQUIRE to work correctly?
option_b: Two CONSECUTIVE slides that contain matching objects — the Morph algorithm identifies objects with the same name or content and smoothly animates the differences

question: What is the difference between a TRANSITION and an ANIMATION in PowerPoint?
option_a: There is no difference — they are the same
option_b: A transition is a SLIDE-LEVEL effect (plays when moving between slides); an animation is an OBJECT-LEVEL effect (plays on individual objects within a single slide)
option_c: Animations are for images; transitions are for text

question: In Book 5's animation chapter; students learn to create a 'BOUNCING BALL' effect. Which animation category is used?
option_b: Emphasis
option_d: Motion Paths — the ball is animated to follow a drawn path (e.g. an arc or bounce path) around the slide

question: What does clicking 'EFFECT OPTIONS' after selecting an animation allow you to do?
option_b: Customise DIRECTION; SEQUENCE; SOUND; and AFTER-ANIMATION behaviour of the selected animation
option_c: Change the animation type to a different category

question: What does the 'AFTER ANIMATION' setting (in Effect Options → Effect tab) do?
option_b: Controls what happens to the object AFTER the animation completes — options include: Don't Dim; Hide After Animation; Hide on Next Mouse Click; or change to a different colour
option_c: Adds a sound after the animation

question: In PowerPoint; what does the SLIDE MASTER (View → Slide Master) have to do with THEMES?
option_b: The Slide Master is where the THEME is STORED AND EDITED — changes to theme colours; fonts; and layouts on the Slide Master apply to all slides using that layout
option_d: It is the first slide in the presentation

question: What is the purpose of the SLIDE SIZE option (Design → Customise → Slide Size)?
option_b: Changes the DIMENSIONS of all slides (e.g. Standard 4:3; Widescreen 16:9; or custom size in cm/inches) to match the display or print format

question: In Book 5 Chapter 4; the PRACTICAL ACTIVITY asks students to add animations to a presentation about their school. Which sequence is recommended?
option_a: Add all animations before adding content
option_b: First create all slides and add content; THEN apply a theme; THEN add transitions; THEN add animations to objects — in that logical build order
option_d: Start with animations; then add text

question: What is the PRESENTER VIEW in PowerPoint (used during a slideshow)?
option_a: A view that shows all slides at once
option_b: A special view that shows the CURRENT SLIDE on the audience screen while the presenter sees the current slide; NEXT SLIDE PREVIEW; speaker notes; and a timer on their own screen
option_d: A view that hides the animations

question: To REMOVE ALL ANIMATIONS from a slide quickly?
option_a: Delete each animation one by one
option_b: Select all objects on the slide (Ctrl+A) → in the Animations tab; select 'None' from the Animation gallery → this removes all animations from all selected objects

question: What type of ENTRANCE animation is 'APPEAR' in PowerPoint?
option_a: The object flies in from the side
option_b: The object INSTANTLY becomes visible on the slide with NO animation motion — the simplest entrance animation
option_d: The object bounces onto the slide

question: What category is the 'SPIN' animation in PowerPoint?
option_a: Entrance (makes the object appear by spinning)
option_b: Exit (makes the object disappear by spinning)
option_c: EMPHASIS — the object is already on the slide; it spins to draw attention; then stays on the slide

question: What does the 'FADE' transition do in PowerPoint?
option_a: Wipes across from left to right
option_b: The current slide GRADUALLY BECOMES TRANSPARENT while the next slide GRADUALLY BECOMES OPAQUE — a smooth dissolve between slides
option_c: Flips the slide like a page turn
option_d: Pushes the slide off the screen

question: What does the 'PUSH' transition do?
option_b: The next slide PUSHES the current slide off the screen from one direction (left; right; up; or down)

question: What is the 'CHECKERBOARD' transition effect in PowerPoint?
option_b: An exciting transition where the slide breaks into a CHECKERBOARD PATTERN of squares that alternate between old and new slides
option_c: A wipe from left to right

question: What type of presentations are DYNAMIC CONTENT transitions most suitable for?
option_b: Presentations where the slide BACKGROUND STAYS FIXED while only the CONTENT (text; images) animates in — giving the impression of continuous flowing content

question: What is the CUBE transition?
option_a: The slide breaks into a checkerboard
option_b: The slide appears to ROTATE ON A 3D CUBE — the current slide rotates away and the next slide rotates into view on an adjacent face
option_c: The slide flips like a book page

question: What does the 'REVEAL' transition do in PowerPoint?
option_b: The current slide is WIPED AWAY like a curtain to REVEAL the next slide underneath
option_d: The slide rotates on a vertical axis

question: What is the GALLERY transition in PowerPoint?
option_b: A transition that makes slides appear to flip like PAGES IN A GALLERY or magazine — with a 3D side-panel sliding effect
option_d: A transition that shows all slides at once

question: In the Animation Pane; what does a GREEN bar represent?
option_b: An emphasis animation
option_c: An ENTRANCE animation — the object appears on the slide when this animation plays

question: In the Animation Pane; what does a RED bar represent?
option_b: Emphasis animation
option_d: EXIT animation — the object leaves the slide when this animation plays

question: What does 'BY 1ST LEVEL PARAGRAPHS' mean in Text Animation (Effect Options)?
option_a: The entire text box appears at once
option_b: Each FIRST-LEVEL BULLET POINT (paragraph) is animated separately — so the presenter can reveal the text one bullet at a time
option_c: Only the first bullet is animated
option_d: The title and subtitle animate together

question: What does 'AS ONE OBJECT' mean in Text Animation (Effect Options)?
option_a: All text animates word by word
option_b: The ENTIRE text box (all paragraphs/bullets) is treated as ONE unit and animates together in a single animation event

question: What does 'BY LETTER' animation sequence mean?
option_b: Each individual CHARACTER (letter) in the text flies in or fades in separately — creating a typewriter or showering effect
option_d: The text box is split into rows

question: To CHANGE THE ORDER of animations in the Animation Pane; you?
option_a: Right-click and choose Move to Top
option_b: Select the animation in the pane then click the UP or DOWN ARROW buttons at the top of the Animation Pane to reorder it
option_c: Drag and drop within the Animation Pane (also works)
option_d: Delete and recreate in the correct order

question: What is 'WIPE' as a PowerPoint transition?
option_b: The new slide is REVEALED gradually by a line sweeping across from one direction (e.g. left to right) — the old slide is wiped away as the new one appears

question: What is 'SPLIT' as a transition in PowerPoint?
option_a: The slide is divided into random shapes
option_b: The slide opens from the centre outward (or closes to centre) either HORIZONTALLY or VERTICALLY — revealing the next slide

question: What does the 'DRAPE' transition do in PowerPoint?
option_b: The slide appears to FOLD AND DRAPE like a curtain or fabric falling — a dramatic textured transition in the Exciting category
option_d: The slide tiles into smaller pieces

question: To add a SOUND to a specific ANIMATION (not a transition); you?
option_b: Animation → Effect Options → Effect tab → SOUND dropdown — choose a built-in sound or browse for a sound file

question: What does the 'GROW/SHRINK' emphasis animation do?
option_a: Moves the object to a new position
option_b: SCALES the object UP (grows) or DOWN (shrinks) by a percentage — drawing attention by temporarily enlarging or reducing it
option_d: Spins the object around its centre

question: What does the 'PULSE' emphasis animation do?
option_a: The object fades out then back
option_b: The object RAPIDLY SCALES UP then back to original size — a quick pulsing beat that draws the eye
option_d: The object slides to a new position

question: What does the 'TEETER' emphasis animation do?
option_b: Makes the object rotate back and forth LIKE A ROCKING OR TEETERING MOTION — a slight side-to-side rotation that draws attention

question: What is the 'BOUNCE' entrance animation?
option_a: The object fades in from top
option_b: The object FLIES IN from outside the slide and BOUNCES a few times before settling in its final position — as if it dropped and bounced like a ball

question: What is the 'ZOOM' entrance animation?
option_a: The object slides in from the left
option_b: The object GROWS from a tiny point to full size AT ITS POSITION on the slide — appearing to zoom toward the viewer

question: What is the 'FLY IN' entrance animation in PowerPoint?
option_b: The object FLIES IN FROM OUTSIDE THE SLIDE (default: from the bottom) and moves to its position on the slide
option_c: The object fades from 0% to 100% opacity

question: What does the 'FLOAT IN' entrance animation do?
option_a: Exactly the same as Fly In
option_b: The object APPEARS ABOVE ITS FINAL POSITION and FLOATS DOWN (or up) gently to settle in place — a softer; more graceful version of Fly In
option_d: The object appears with a bounce

question: What is the 'SWIVEL' entrance animation?
option_b: The object appears to SPIN ON A VERTICAL OR HORIZONTAL AXIS — rotating into view from an edge as if mounted on a hinge
option_d: The object grows from a point

question: In Book 5; students learn to use SOUND EFFECTS with transitions. What format does PowerPoint prefer for transition sounds?
option_b: WAV — the standard uncompressed audio format compatible with PowerPoint transition sound effects

question: A student has applied a 'FLY IN' animation to a title text and the text appears all at once. She wants each WORD to fly in separately. She should?
option_b: Change Effect Options → Sequence → 'BY WORD' — this makes each word in the text animate separately in sequence

question: What does the 'PATH POINTS' edit mode allow you to do for a Custom Motion Path?
option_b: RESHAPE the motion path by dragging its anchor points — add; delete; or move points to create curves and corners in the path

question: Which of the following animations would be BEST for making a company LOGO gradually appear on a title slide?
option_b: Appear Entrance (no movement; just instant reveal)
option_c: Fade Entrance — a professional; subtle appearance that draws attention without distraction

question: What does 'HIDE AFTER ANIMATION' (Effect Options → After animation) do?
option_b: The object BECOMES INVISIBLE immediately after its animation completes — useful for making content disappear after being revealed
option_c: The object moves off the slide

question: What is the purpose of NAMED OBJECTS in the Selection Pane for the Morph transition?
option_b: To give objects CONSISTENT NAMES across two consecutive slides so PowerPoint can match them and animate the differences smoothly using Morph

question: A student applies a theme and realises the BACKGROUND COLOUR is not ideal. Without changing the entire theme; she can?
option_b: Go to Design → Customise → Format Background → change only the background fill (solid; gradient; picture) while keeping all other theme settings
option_c: Change the text colours in Home

question: What does 'REVERSE PATH DIRECTION' do for a Motion Path animation?
option_b: Makes the object travel the path in the OPPOSITE DIRECTION — start point becomes end point; end becomes start

question: What happens to an object set to 'HIDE ON NEXT MOUSE CLICK' after animation?
option_b: The object STAYS VISIBLE after its animation but DISAPPEARS when the presenter makes the next mouse click (or keypress)

question: In Book 5; students create a QUIZ slide using animations. What technique is taught for REVEALING ANSWERS one at a time?
option_b: Animate each answer text with Start: On Click so each presenter click reveals the next answer option progressively
option_c: Put all answers in a table

question: A student applies FIVE different transitions to FIVE slides. She later decides all slides should have the SAME FADE transition. What is the fastest method?
option_a: Delete all transitions and redo them
option_b: Apply Fade to slide 1; select all slides in Slide Sorter view (Ctrl+A); then click Apply to All in the Transitions tab

question: What view in PowerPoint is BEST for managing and reordering slides while checking which transitions are applied?
option_b: Reading View
option_c: SLIDE SORTER VIEW (View → Slide Sorter) — shows all slide thumbnails with transition icons below each; and allows drag-and-drop reordering

question: In PowerPoint 2016; what does pressing F5 do during a presentation?
option_b: Starts the SLIDESHOW FROM THE FIRST SLIDE — the presentation goes full-screen from slide 1
option_d: Starts the slideshow from the current slide

question: What does pressing SHIFT+F5 do in PowerPoint?
option_b: Starts the slideshow FROM THE CURRENT SLIDE (not from slide 1) — useful for testing the current slide without going back to the beginning

question: What does ESCAPE (Esc) do when pressed during a PowerPoint slideshow?
option_b: Ends the slideshow and RETURNS TO NORMAL EDITING VIEW — the current slide stays selected

question: What does the 'HIDE SLIDE' feature do in PowerPoint?
option_b: MARKS A SLIDE so it is SKIPPED during the normal slideshow — the slide stays in the file but does not appear when pressing Next. It can be shown by typing its slide number during the show

question: What is the 'SCREEN RECORDING' feature in PowerPoint 2016 used for?
option_b: Recording the COMPUTER SCREEN and inserting the recording directly onto a slide as a video object

question: What is the difference between 'LOOP CONTINUOUSLY UNTIL ESC' and a fixed repeat count for an animation?
option_b: Loop Continuously keeps repeating the animation INDEFINITELY until Esc is pressed or until another trigger fires; a fixed count repeats it exactly N times then stops

question: What does 'SMOOTH START' and 'SMOOTH END' do in animation Effect Options Timing?
option_b: Causes the animation to START SLOWLY then speed up (Smooth Start) or SLOW DOWN before stopping (Smooth End) — creating a more natural; eased movement

question: In Book 5; students apply a theme to a presentation. After applying the theme; the teacher tells them to check that ALL TEXT IS STILL READABLE. Why might text become HARD TO READ after applying a theme?
option_b: A theme changes the slide BACKGROUND COLOUR — if existing text is dark on a white background; a theme with a dark background makes dark text invisible against dark
option_d: The theme changes font to white on white

question: What is the ANIMATION PAINTER keyboard shortcut in PowerPoint?
option_a: There is no keyboard shortcut — only the toolbar button (double-click for multiple applications)
option_b: Ctrl+Shift+C

question: A student wants a PHOTO to stay HIDDEN; then APPEAR only when she clicks during her presentation. Which animation should she apply to the photo?
option_b: Emphasis → Spin
option_c: ENTRANCE → APPEAR (or Fade) with Start: On Click — the photo is invisible initially and appears when clicked

question: What does 'REWIND WHEN DONE PLAYING' do for an animation?
option_b: After the animation completes; the OBJECT RETURNS TO ITS ORIGINAL STARTING STATE — useful for Motion Paths where you want the object to 'snap back' to its starting position after moving

question: In Book 5 Chapter 4; what is the RECOMMENDATION about how many animations to use per slide for a professional presentation?
option_a: As many as possible — more is better
option_b: Use at MOST 2–3 animations per slide; focusing on animations that serve a purpose (revealing content gradually; emphasising key points) rather than decorating with effects for their own sake

question: What is the 'ORIGAMI' transition in PowerPoint 2016?
option_b: An Exciting category transition that makes the slide appear to FOLD like origami paper into a new shape revealing the next slide

question: What is a CUSTOM SLIDE SHOW in PowerPoint (Slide Show → Custom Slide Show)?
option_b: A SAVED SUBSET of slides from the full presentation that can be run independently — useful for presenting different versions to different audiences without maintaining separate files
option_d: A slideshow with custom animations only

question: What is the PHOTO ALBUM feature in PowerPoint 2016?
option_a: A feature to create slideshows of internet images
option_b: A built-in tool (Insert → Photo Album → New Photo Album) that automatically creates a new presentation with one or more photos per slide — imported from folders on the computer
option_c: A feature to add a photo to a slide background
option_d: A feature to organise files in a folder

question: To INSERT A PHOTO ALBUM in PowerPoint 2016; you go to?
option_b: Insert → Photo Album → New Photo Album

question: In the Photo Album dialog; what PICTURE LAYOUT options are available?
option_b: Fit to slide; 1 picture; 2 pictures; 4 pictures; 1 picture with title; 2 pictures with title; 4 pictures with title

question: What does the 'ALL PICTURES BLACK AND WHITE' checkbox do in the Photo Album dialog?
option_a: Prints the photos in black and white
option_b: Converts ALL IMPORTED PHOTOS to greyscale (black and white) in the presentation — a quick effect without editing each photo individually
option_d: Adds a black frame to each photo

question: What is the PURPOSE of the FRAME SHAPE option in the Photo Album dialog?
option_a: Adds a digital frame to the presentation background
option_b: Applies a decorative border shape (Rectangle; Rounded Rectangle; Simple Frame; Shadow Frame; Soft Edge Rectangle; etc.) to EACH PHOTO in the album
option_d: Adds a text box around each photo

question: What does the 'CAPTIONS BELOW ALL PICTURES' option do in Photo Album?
option_b: Adds a TEXT PLACEHOLDER BELOW EACH PHOTO where you can type a caption for each picture after the album is created

question: To EDIT AN EXISTING Photo Album in PowerPoint?
option_b: Insert → Photo Album → EDIT PHOTO ALBUM — reopens the Photo Album dialog with the current settings allowing you to add/remove photos; change layout; or update frames
option_c: Double-click a photo in the album

question: In the Photo Album dialog; the UP and DOWN ARROW buttons are used to?
option_b: REORDER the selected photo in the photo list — moving it higher or lower in the sequence of slides

question: Which BRIGHTNESS and CONTRAST tools appear in the Photo Album dialog?
option_b: Six small BUTTONS below the preview: decrease/increase Brightness (sun icons) and decrease/increase Contrast (circle icons); plus Rotate Left/Rotate Right

question: What file types can be inserted as AUDIO in a PowerPoint 2016 presentation?
option_b: WAV files only
option_c: MP3; WAV; WMA; MIDI; AIFF; AU; and other common audio formats
option_d: Only audio bought from the Microsoft Store

question: To INSERT AUDIO (background music or narration) in PowerPoint 2016?
option_b: Insert → Audio → AUDIO ON MY PC (browse for a local file) or RECORD AUDIO (record directly with a microphone)

question: After inserting audio; the AUDIO TOOLS tabs appear. What are they called?
option_b: Design and Layout
option_c: FORMAT and PLAYBACK — Format handles the audio icon appearance; Playback handles how/when audio plays

question: What does the 'HIDE DURING SHOW' option do for an audio file?
option_b: Hides the audio WAVEFORM display on the slide
option_c: Hides the SPEAKER ICON on the slide during the slideshow so the audience does not see it

question: What does 'PLAY ACROSS SLIDES' mean for an audio file in PowerPoint?
option_a: The audio plays on one slide only
option_b: The audio CONTINUES PLAYING as the presentation advances through MULTIPLE slides without stopping — useful for background music throughout the presentation
option_c: The audio plays on every other slide
option_d: The audio loops on the current slide

question: What does 'LOOP UNTIL STOPPED' do for audio in PowerPoint?
option_b: Makes the audio FILE REPEAT CONTINUOUSLY from the beginning when it ends — so background music keeps playing as long as the slide (or presentation) is shown

question: To TRIM AN AUDIO FILE in PowerPoint (removing the start or end)?
option_b: Audio Tools Playback → TRIM AUDIO — opens a dialog with a waveform and sliders to set a new start time and end time for the clip (the original file is unchanged)
option_c: Delete and reinsert a shorter clip

question: What does the START dropdown (On Click or Automatically) control for audio in PowerPoint?
option_b: The volume fade
option_c: When the audio BEGINS PLAYING — 'On Click' waits for a mouse click; 'Automatically' plays the audio as soon as the slide appears

question: What file types can be inserted as VIDEO in PowerPoint 2016?
option_b: Only .MP4
option_c: MP4; WMV; AVI; MOV; MPG; SWF (Flash; limited) and other common video formats

question: To INSERT A VIDEO FILE from your computer in PowerPoint 2016?

question: After inserting a video; what TWO contextual tabs appear in the ribbon?

question: What does 'PLAY FULL SCREEN' do for a video in PowerPoint?

question: What does 'REWIND AFTER PLAYING' do for a video in PowerPoint?

question: To set a POSTER FRAME (a thumbnail image shown for the video before it plays) in PowerPoint?

question: To TRIM A VIDEO in PowerPoint (play only a portion of it)?

question: What does SLIDE SHOW → SET UP SLIDE SHOW control?

question: What does the 'BROWSED AT A KIOSK' show type do in Set Up Slide Show?

question: What is the 'REHEARSE TIMINGS' feature in PowerPoint?

question: What is the purpose of 'RECORD SLIDE SHOW' in PowerPoint 2016?

question: What is the file extension for a POWERPOINT SHOW file (a file that opens directly in Slideshow mode)?

question: To save a presentation as a POWERPOINT SHOW (.ppsx) file?

option_b: File → Export → Create PDF

question: What is the PRESENTER VIEW in PowerPoint (Slide Show → Presenter View)?

question: What does the 'LOOP CONTINUOUSLY UNTIL ESC' checkbox do in Set Up Slide Show?

question: What does the 'SHOW WITHOUT NARRATION' checkbox do in Set Up Slide Show?

question: What is an 'ONLINE PRESENTATION' in PowerPoint 2016?

option_d: Embedding the file in a website

question: To ADD SPEAKER NOTES to a slide in PowerPoint?

question: What does PRINT → NOTES PAGES print in PowerPoint?

question: What does 'HANDOUTS' print in PowerPoint?

question: What is OUTLINE VIEW in PowerPoint?

question: What is the purpose of the LASER POINTER during a slideshow in PowerPoint?

question: What does the PEN tool do during a slideshow in PowerPoint?

question: To INSERT ONLINE VIDEO (from YouTube) into a PowerPoint slide?

question: What does 'EMBED VIDEO' mean vs 'LINK TO VIDEO' in PowerPoint?

question: What is the 'COMPRESS MEDIA' feature in PowerPoint (File → Info → Compress Media)?

question: What does the EXPORT TO VIDEO feature do in PowerPoint 2016?
option_a: Embeds a video on a slide

question: What RESOLUTION options are available when exporting a presentation as video in PowerPoint?
option_b: Ultra HD (4K); Full HD (1080p); HD (720p); and Standard (480p)

question: After exporting to VIDEO; an audience member can watch the PowerPoint presentation?

question: What is the purpose of the 'SECTIONS' feature in PowerPoint?

question: In Book 5 Chapter 5; what TYPE OF PRESENTATION do students build using Photo Album; audio; and slideshow features?

question: What does the 'SLIDE SHOW' tab → 'HIDE SLIDE' do to a presentation?

question: To navigate DIRECTLY TO A SPECIFIC SLIDE during a running slideshow?

question: What is the 'BLACK SCREEN' shortcut during a PowerPoint slideshow?
option_b: B or . (full stop) — pressing B or period makes the screen go BLACK; hiding the current slide from the audience (press again to return to the slide)

question: In Book 5; students learn to save a presentation as PDF. What is the advantage of PDF over PPSX?
option_b: A PDF DOES NOT REQUIRE POWERPOINT to open — it shows slides as fixed images in any PDF viewer; on any device; with no animation or interactivity but guaranteed visual fidelity

question: What is a CUSTOM SLIDE SHOW in PowerPoint?

question: What keyboard shortcut STARTS a PowerPoint slideshow from SLIDE 1?
option_b: F5 — starts from the very first slide regardless of which slide is currently selected

question: What keyboard shortcut STARTS a PowerPoint slideshow from the CURRENT SLIDE?

question: To ADD AUDIO that plays AUTOMATICALLY when a specific slide appears?
option_b: Insert → Audio → Audio on My PC → after inserting; set Audio Tools Playback → Start → Automatically

question: What is the AUDIO ICON that appears on a slide after inserting audio?

question: To make background music FADE IN at the beginning of an audio clip in PowerPoint?

question: What is the VOLUME control for audio in PowerPoint's Playback tab?

question: What file format does PowerPoint EXPORT to when creating a video using 'Create a Video' (File → Export)?
option_b: .mp4 (MPEG-4 Video) or .wmv (Windows Media Video) — both are standard video formats

question: When inserting a VIDEO from a local file; what does PowerPoint do with the video file by DEFAULT?
option_b: EMBEDS it inside the .pptx file — the video data is copied into the presentation so it plays even if the original video file is deleted or moved

question: What SECTION of the RIBBON appears when you click on an embedded VIDEO object on a slide?
option_b: Drawing Tools
option_c: Video Tools — with FORMAT and PLAYBACK tabs that are specific to video objects

question: What does 'HIDE WHILE NOT PLAYING' do for a video in PowerPoint?
option_b: Makes the VIDEO INVISIBLE on the slide EXCEPT when it is actively playing — the slide shows a blank space in the video's position between playbacks
option_c: Hides the video from the slide panel
option_d: Removes the video from the file

question: What does the DURATION field in the TRANSITIONS tab control?
option_b: The LENGTH OF TIME (in seconds) the transition ANIMATION takes to complete — for example; a Duration of 01.00 means the transition takes one second
option_d: The time before the transition starts

question: What is the MORPH TRANSITION in PowerPoint 2016?
option_b: A SMART TRANSITION that moves; scales; and transforms objects that appear on BOTH the current and next slide — creates smooth animated motion without complex animation settings

question: For MORPH transition to work correctly with text or images; what must be TRUE about objects on consecutive slides?
option_a: They must have the same font
option_b: Objects must share the SAME NAME in the Selection Pane (Format → Arrange → Selection Pane → rename objects) OR be duplicated slides — Morph then knows which object maps to which

option_d: They must be in the same position

question: What is SLIDE SORTER VIEW in PowerPoint (View → Slide Sorter)?
option_a: A view for editing slide content

question: What keyboard shortcut DUPLICATES a slide in PowerPoint?
option_b: CTRL+D — duplicates the selected slide(s) as a copy inserted immediately after the selected slide

question: What does 'APPLY TO ALL' in the Transitions tab do?
option_b: Applies the SELECTED TRANSITION (including its settings: effect options; duration; sound; advance timing) to EVERY SLIDE in the presentation — a one-click way to set a consistent transition throughout
option_c: Applies the theme to all slides
option_d: Applies the layout to all slides

question: What is the READING VIEW in PowerPoint?
option_b: A simplified SLIDESHOW VIEW within the PowerPoint window (not full-screen) — useful for reviewing the presentation with all animations and transitions playing; without switching to full-screen mode
option_c: A view that shows only text

question: What does FILE → INFO → CHECK COMPATIBILITY do in PowerPoint 2016?
option_b: Checks whether the presentation uses features that are NOT supported by OLDER versions of PowerPoint (2003; 2007; 2010) — and lists any potential issues
option_c: Checks if the file is corrupted

question: What does 'INSPECT DOCUMENT' (File → Info → Check for Issues → Inspect Document) do?
option_b: Searches for HIDDEN DATA in the presentation — such as speaker notes; comments; hidden slides; author metadata; personal information; and invisible objects — so you can remove them before sharing

question: What PRINT LAYOUT prints slides with LINES for audience notes in PowerPoint?

question: What is the DEFAULT FILE FORMAT for saving a PowerPoint 2016 presentation?

question: In the Photo Album dialog; what is 'FIT TO SLIDE' layout?

question: What type of audio file is BEST for background music in a PowerPoint presentation?

question: To INSERT AUDIO FROM A MICROPHONE directly in PowerPoint without a separate app?

option_b: Insert → Microphone

question: After recording audio with 'Record Audio' in PowerPoint; where does the audio appear?
option_b: As a SPEAKER ICON on the slide — the same as any other embedded audio; with the same Audio Tools FORMAT and PLAYBACK tabs available

question: To REORDER photos in a Photo Album AFTER the album has been created?

question: What does SLIDE SHOW → PLAY NARRATIONS checkbox control?

question: In Book 5; students learn to insert a VIDEO from their computer. What FORMAT is recommended for reliable playback in PowerPoint 2016?

question: What happens when you DOUBLE-CLICK a .ppsx file in Windows?

question: What does the SCREEN RECORDING feature do in PowerPoint 2016 (Insert → Screen Recording)?

question: What does clicking 'SAVE AS' (.ppsx) do differently from normal 'SAVE' (.pptx) in PowerPoint?
option_b: Creates a FILE THAT OPENS DIRECTLY IN SLIDESHOW MODE — saved as a PowerPoint Show (.ppsx) rather than an editable presentation (.pptx)

question: What SLIDE SHOW → MONITOR setting does when you have TWO DISPLAYS connected?

question: What is the purpose of the TIMER DISPLAY in Presenter View during a slideshow?

question: In Book 5's practical exercise; students create a multimedia presentation. What is the CORRECT ORDER of steps?

question: What is a TRANSITION SOUND in PowerPoint (Transitions → Timing → Sound)?

question: What does 'ADVANCE SLIDE: AFTER' (a set time) do in the Transitions tab?

question: What is the purpose of LINKING a video file in PowerPoint (rather than embedding it)?

question: What does the REMOVE BACKGROUND feature do in PowerPoint (available for images via Picture Tools → Format → Remove Background)?
option_b: Automatically removes the background from a PHOTO on a slide — keeping the main subject and making the rest transparent — using AI-based detection with pink highlights

question: When a SLIDE TRANSITION is set to 'ON MOUSE CLICK' and the presenter presses the SPACEBAR during a show; what happens?
option_b: The spacebar ADVANCES the slide — it acts like a mouse click; progressing to the next slide or the next animation on the current slide

question: What does pressing RIGHT ARROW key do during a PowerPoint slideshow?
option_b: Advances to the next slide or next animation — the same as a mouse click or spacebar press

question: What VIEW shows ALL SLIDES as equal-sized thumbnails and is most useful for REORDERING a long presentation?
option_b: Outline view

question: What does the PAPER CLIP icon on a slide thumbnail in the slide panel indicate in PowerPoint?

question: What is the INTERNET?
option_a: A single computer owned by a company
option_b: A GLOBAL NETWORK of millions of interconnected computers and devices that share information and resources using agreed-upon protocols (rules)
option_d: A wireless signal from a router

question: What is the WORLD WIDE WEB (WWW)?
option_b: A COLLECTION OF WEBSITES and web pages stored on web servers and accessed via the Internet using a web browser — it is only one part of the Internet
option_c: A type of cable used to connect computers

question: What is a WEB BROWSER?
option_b: A SOFTWARE APPLICATION (e.g. Microsoft Edge; Google Chrome; Mozilla Firefox; Safari) used to ACCESS and DISPLAY websites and web pages on the Internet

question: What is MICROSOFT EDGE?
option_b: Microsoft's built-in WEB BROWSER included with Windows 10 and 11 — it replaced Internet Explorer as Microsoft's default browser; built on the Chromium engine

question: What is a URL (Uniform Resource Locator)?
option_b: The UNIQUE WEB ADDRESS of a page or resource on the Internet — for example: https://www.bbc.com/news — that browsers use to locate and retrieve it

question: What does HTTP stand for?
option_a: HyperText Transfer Protocol — the rules for transmitting web pages between servers and browsers over the Internet
option_b: High Transfer Text Protocol

question: What does HTTPS mean and why is it important?
option_b: HyperText Transfer Protocol SECURE — an ENCRYPTED version of HTTP that protects data exchanged between your browser and the web server using SSL/TLS; shown as a padlock in the address bar

question: What is a SEARCH ENGINE?
option_a: A website that stores files for download
option_b: A WEB SERVICE (e.g. Google; Bing; Yahoo) that crawls the Internet to index web pages and then lets users find relevant pages by typing SEARCH QUERIES (keywords)

question: What is GOOGLE?
option_b: A file storage service
option_c: The world's most popular SEARCH ENGINE — accessed at www.google.com — that uses complex algorithms to rank billions of web pages by relevance to search queries

question: What is MICROSOFT BING?
option_b: Microsoft's SEARCH ENGINE (www.bing.com) — built into Windows and Microsoft Edge as the default search engine; with features like image search; video search; and news search

question: In the Microsoft Edge ADDRESS BAR; you can BOTH type a URL to go directly to a website AND type a search query. When you type a search term without a URL; Edge does what?
option_b: Sends the search query to the DEFAULT SEARCH ENGINE (Bing by default in Edge; or whichever is set) and shows results

question: What is the HOMEPAGE in a web browser?
option_b: The WEB PAGE that opens automatically when you launch the browser or click the Home button — set in browser Settings

question: What is a FAVOURITE / BOOKMARK in a web browser?
option_b: A SAVED SHORTCUT to a website or web page that lets you return to it quickly without retyping the URL — saved via the star icon in Edge or Ctrl+D

question: What does the BACK BUTTON (←) do in a web browser?
option_b: Goes BACK to the PREVIOUS web page in the current tab's history

question: What does the REFRESH / RELOAD button do in a web browser?
option_a: Goes back to the previous page
option_b: RE-LOADS the CURRENT web page — downloading a fresh copy from the server; updating any content that may have changed since the page was last loaded

question: What is a BROWSER TAB?
option_b: A SEPARATE BROWSING SESSION within the same browser window — each tab shows an independent web page; letting you open multiple websites simultaneously without opening multiple windows
option_c: A section of a web page

question: What keyboard shortcut opens a NEW TAB in most web browsers?
option_b: Ctrl+T — opens a new empty tab in the same browser window

question: What does CTRL+W do in a web browser?
option_b: Closes the CURRENT TAB

question: What is PRIVATE BROWSING (InPrivate in Edge; Incognito in Chrome)?
option_a: Browsing that is invisible to the internet
option_b: A BROWSING MODE where the browser does NOT save the browsing history; cookies; form data; or passwords from that session — closed when the window is closed

question: To open an INCOGNITO window in Microsoft Edge (called InPrivate)?
option_b: Ctrl+Shift+N — opens a new InPrivate (private browsing) window where browsing history; cookies; and site data are not saved locally

question: What is an EMAIL ADDRESS? Give an example of its structure.
option_b: A unique IDENTIFIER for an email account in the format: username@domain.com — for example: student@school.edu — where @ separates the username from the domain

question: What is CYBERBULLYING?
option_b: Using digital technology (social media; messaging; gaming; email) to REPEATEDLY HARASS; THREATEN; HUMILIATE; or EMBARRASS another person — a form of bullying that occurs online or via devices

question: What should you do if you experience or witness CYBERBULLYING?
option_b: DO NOT respond to the bully; SAVE EVIDENCE (screenshots); BLOCK the bully; and TELL A TRUSTED ADULT (parent; teacher; school counsellor) immediately

question: What is a PHISHING ATTACK?
option_b: A FRAUDULENT ATTEMPT to steal personal information (passwords; credit card numbers; etc.) by disguising as a TRUSTWORTHY source — usually through fake emails; websites; or messages that look legitimate
option_d: A way to speed up internet connections

question: What is SPAM?
option_b: UNSOLICITED (unwanted) BULK EMAIL — usually commercial advertising; scams; or phishing attempts — sent to large numbers of recipients without their consent

question: What is MALWARE?
option_b: Malicious Software — programs designed to HARM; DISRUPT; or GAIN UNAUTHORISED ACCESS to a computer system — types include viruses; worms; Trojans; ransomware; and spyware

question: What is a COMPUTER VIRUS?
option_b: A TYPE OF MALWARE that ATTACHES ITSELF to legitimate files and REPLICATES — spreading to other files and computers when infected files are shared; it can damage data; slow the system; or cause other harm

question: What is ANTIVIRUS SOFTWARE?
option_a: Software that speeds up the internet
option_b: A SECURITY PROGRAM that detects; prevents; and removes malware (viruses; worms; Trojans; etc.) from a computer — examples include Windows Defender; Avast; Norton; and Kaspersky

question: What is a STRONG PASSWORD? Which of these is strongest?
option_b: password2024
option_c: P@55w0rd!#X9qR — long; uses uppercase; lowercase; numbers; and special characters; making it very hard to guess or crack

question: What is TWO-FACTOR AUTHENTICATION (2FA)?
option_b: A SECURITY METHOD that requires TWO forms of verification to log in — typically a PASSWORD (something you know) plus a SECOND FACTOR such as a code sent to your phone (something you have)

question: Why should you NEVER share personal information (full name; address; phone; school name) with strangers ONLINE?
option_a: Because it is against the law
option_b: Because strangers online may not be who they claim to be — sharing personal information with strangers online puts you at risk of identity theft; stalking; fraud; or other harms
option_c: Because the internet is always slow

question: What does CTRL+F do in a WEB BROWSER or document?
option_a: Finds (SEARCHES) for a word or phrase within the current web page or document — opens a search bar where you type the text and the browser highlights all matching instances on the page
option_b: Opens Favourites

question: To DOWNLOAD A FILE from the Internet in Edge or Chrome?
option_a: Right-click the file link → Save link as (or just click the link and the browser downloads it automatically) to save it to the chosen folder on the computer
option_b: Use Ctrl+S

question: What is an ISP (Internet Service Provider)?
option_b: A COMPANY that provides INTERNET ACCESS to homes; schools; and businesses — examples include local telecom companies; cable providers; and mobile operators

question: What is BANDWIDTH?
option_b: The AMOUNT OF DATA that can be transmitted over an internet connection per second — measured in Mbps (Megabits per second) or Gbps; higher bandwidth means faster internet
option_c: The number of web pages on the Internet
option_d: The strength of a Wi-Fi signal

question: What is WI-FI?
option_b: WIRELESS networking technology that allows devices to connect to the Internet or a local network without physical cables — using radio signals from a WIRELESS ROUTER
option_c: A type of cable for internet

question: What is a HOTSPOT?
option_b: A location or device that provides a PUBLIC or SHARED Wi-Fi internet connection — such as a café; airport; school; or a mobile phone sharing its data connection
option_d: A computer that has a virus

question: Why should you be CAREFUL using PUBLIC Wi-Fi hotspots?
option_b: Because public Wi-Fi is often UNENCRYPTED — anyone nearby can potentially intercept data you send and receive; so never log in to banking; email; or sensitive accounts on unsecured public Wi-Fi

question: What does COOKIES mean in the context of web browsing?
option_b: Small TEXT FILES stored on your computer by websites to REMEMBER information about you — such as login status; shopping cart contents; language preferences; and site settings

question: What is ONLINE SAFETY? Give TWO key rules.
option_b: Behaving responsibly and protecting yourself online — key rules include: (1) Never share personal information with strangers. (2) Tell a trusted adult if something makes you uncomfortable online.

question: What is NETIQUETTE?
option_b: ONLINE ETIQUETTE — the rules of polite; respectful; and responsible behaviour when communicating online (messaging; email; social media; forums)

question: What is a HYPERLINK?
option_b: A CLICKABLE LINK on a web page — usually formatted as underlined coloured text or an image — that navigates to another web page; document; or resource when clicked

question: What is CLOUD STORAGE?
option_b: Online storage services (e.g. OneDrive; Google Drive; iCloud) that store files on REMOTE SERVERS accessed via the Internet — letting you access files from any device anywhere
option_c: A type of physical hard drive

question: What is STREAMING?
option_b: Receiving and playing AUDIO or VIDEO in real time over the Internet WITHOUT DOWNLOADING the file first — examples: YouTube; Netflix; Spotify

question: What is SOCIAL MEDIA? Give an example.
option_b: Online PLATFORMS that let users CREATE and SHARE CONTENT and INTERACT with others — examples include Facebook; Instagram; TikTok; Twitter/X; Snapchat; YouTube

question: In Microsoft Edge; what is the READING VIEW?

question: What does DOWNLOADING mean?
option_a: Sending a file to the internet
option_b: Transferring a FILE from the INTERNET (a server) to YOUR COMPUTER — saving a local copy

question: What does UPLOADING mean?
option_b: Transferring files FROM YOUR COMPUTER to a server on the Internet — for example; sending a photo to social media; submitting work to a class website; or saving a file to cloud storage

question: Why is it important to EVALUATE THE RELIABILITY of websites found via search engines?
option_a: Because search engines rank paid sites first

question: What does the PADLOCK ICON in the browser address bar mean?

option_d: The website is safe to download from

question: To SEARCH EFFECTIVELY with Google; what does putting a phrase in QUOTATION MARKS do?
option_b: Forces an EXACT PHRASE MATCH — only pages containing that EXACT phrase in that EXACT ORDER appear in results — useful for finding specific quotes; titles; or multi-word terms

question: What does using a MINUS SIGN in a Google search do (e.g. 'jaguars -cars')?
option_b: EXCLUDES pages containing the word after the minus sign — 'jaguars -cars' finds pages about Jaguar animals; excluding pages about Jaguar cars

question: To search ONLY within a specific WEBSITE using Google?
option_a: Click 'Search this site' on the page
option_b: Type 'site:website.com your search terms' in Google — e.g. 'site:bbc.com climate change' searches only the BBC website for 'climate change'
option_d: Use the website's own search box only

question: What is the DIFFERENCE between a SEARCH ENGINE and a WEB BROWSER?
option_b: A BROWSER is an application that displays web pages (Edge; Chrome; Firefox); a SEARCH ENGINE is a website/service that helps you FIND web pages (Google; Bing) — you use a browser to access a search engine
option_d: A browser can only open local files

question: What is a DOMAIN NAME in a URL? (e.g. 'google.com' in 'https://www.google.com/search')
option_a: The name of the web browser
option_b: The HUMAN-READABLE ADDRESS of a website (google.com; bbc.co.uk; etc.) that is translated by DNS into the numeric IP address of the server hosting the site
option_c: The folder path after the first slash

question: What does '.com' in a domain name indicate?
option_b: A COMMERCIAL organisation — '.com' is the most common top-level domain (TLD); originally for US commercial entities but now used worldwide by any organisation

question: What does '.edu' or '.ac.uk' in a domain name indicate?
option_b: A government website
option_c: An EDUCATIONAL or ACADEMIC institution — making it a reliable source for academic information

question: What is an IP ADDRESS?
option_b: A NUMERICAL LABEL (e.g. 192.168.1.1) assigned to every device on a network — the actual address computers use to find and communicate with each other on the Internet
option_d: A login name for a website

question: What is DNS (Domain Name System)?
option_b: The INTERNET'S 'PHONE BOOK' — a distributed system that translates HUMAN-READABLE domain names (google.com) into MACHINE-READABLE IP addresses so browsers can connect to the right servers

question: What is a WEB SERVER?
option_b: A COMPUTER that stores website files and sends them to browsers that request them — web servers run 24/7 and respond to HTTP/HTTPS requests from users worldwide

question: What does 'CACHE' mean in web browsing?
option_b: STORED COPIES of web pages; images; and files saved LOCALLY on your computer by the browser so that frequently visited pages load FASTER on repeat visits

question: What does CLEARING THE BROWSER CACHE do?
option_b: Removes LOCALLY STORED COPIES of web pages and media files — the browser must re-download fresh copies from the server; which can fix display problems but makes initial page loads slower

question: What is ONLINE PLAGIARISM?
option_b: Copying text; images; or ideas from the Internet and presenting them as YOUR OWN WORK without crediting the original source

question: What is COPYRIGHT? How does it apply to images found on the Internet?
option_a: Copyright means anything on the internet is free to use
option_b: Copyright gives the CREATOR of original work (text; images; music; video) EXCLUSIVE RIGHTS — images found on the Internet are usually protected by copyright and cannot be used without permission or a licence

question: What are CREATIVE COMMONS licences?
option_b: Licences that allow creators to grant PUBLIC PERMISSION to use their work under specific conditions — ranging from free to use for any purpose; to free for non-commercial use only; with or without credit required

question: What is GOOGLE CHROME?
option_b: Google's WEB BROWSER — a free browser developed by Google that is the most widely used browser globally; available for Windows; Mac; iOS; and Android

question: What is the DIFFERENCE between MICROSOFT EDGE and GOOGLE CHROME?
option_b: EDGE is made by MICROSOFT (pre-installed on Windows); CHROME is made by GOOGLE (must be downloaded separately) — both are Chromium-based browsers but are separate products with different features and defaults
option_c: Edge is faster than Chrome always
option_d: Chrome can only be used on Google devices

question: When using a SEARCH ENGINE; what are SPONSORED (AD) RESULTS?
option_b: PAID ADVERTISEMENTS that appear at the TOP of search results — marked as 'Sponsored' or 'Ad' — companies pay the search engine to appear at the top for specific search terms

question: What does 'SAFE SEARCH' do on a search engine?
option_b: FILTERS OUT explicit; adult; or inappropriate content from search results — most search engines offer SafeSearch settings to help filter unwanted content for younger users

question: In Google; how do you search for IMAGES only?
option_b: Click the 'Images' tab at the top of Google search results — this filters results to show only images rather than web pages

question: What is EMAIL (Electronic Mail)?
option_b: A DIGITAL MESSAGING SERVICE that allows text messages; attachments (files; images); and links to be sent between users over the Internet — almost instantly; to anyone in the world with an email address

question: What does CC mean in an email?
option_a: Carbon Copy — ADDITIONAL RECIPIENTS who receive a copy of the email; visible to all other recipients
option_b: Closed Copy

question: What does BCC mean in an email?
option_a: Blind Carbon Copy — sends a copy to additional recipients whose email addresses are HIDDEN from all other recipients
option_b: Big Carbon Copy

question: What is an EMAIL ATTACHMENT?
option_b: A FILE (document; image; PDF; video; etc.) that is ATTACHED to an email message and sent along with it — the recipient can download and open the attached file
option_c: A photo in the email body

question: Why should you NEVER open email attachments from UNKNOWN senders?
option_a: Because the attachment might be large
option_b: Because attachments from unknown senders may contain MALWARE (viruses; Trojans; ransomware) that infect your computer when opened — a common method for spreading malicious software

question: What is RANSOMWARE?
option_b: A type of MALWARE that ENCRYPTS a victim's files and demands a RANSOM PAYMENT to restore access — victims cannot open their own files unless they pay or have backups

question: What is SPYWARE?
option_b: MALWARE that secretly MONITORS and COLLECTS information about a user's activities (keystrokes; passwords; browsing history; financial data) and sends it to a third party WITHOUT the user's knowledge

question: What is a FIREWALL?
option_b: A SECURITY SYSTEM (hardware or software) that MONITORS and CONTROLS incoming and outgoing network traffic based on security rules — blocking unauthorised access to or from a private network

question: What is a VPN (Virtual Private Network)?
option_b: A SERVICE that creates an ENCRYPTED TUNNEL for internet traffic; routing it through a server in another location — hiding the user's real IP address and protecting data from interception

question: What does the term 'GOING VIRAL' mean on the internet?
option_b: When a piece of online CONTENT (video; image; article; meme) SPREADS RAPIDLY across the internet — shared by millions of people in a short time — reaching a huge audience organically
option_d: When a file is uploaded to the internet

question: What is FAKE NEWS?
option_b: FALSE or MISLEADING INFORMATION presented as NEWS — deliberately created to deceive; influence opinion; or spread for entertainment; often shared on social media before being fact-checked

question: What is the purpose of a CAPTCHA on websites?
option_b: To verify that the USER is a HUMAN and not an automated bot — by presenting a challenge (identifying images; distorted text) that is easy for humans but difficult for computer programs to solve

question: What is SCREEN TIME and why is it important to manage it?
option_a: The brightness setting of a screen
option_b: The TOTAL TIME spent looking at digital screens (computers; phones; tablets; TV) — managing screen time is important for eye health; physical activity; sleep quality; and maintaining real-world relationships

question: What is DIGITAL FOOTPRINT?
option_b: The TRAIL OF DATA left by a person's online activities — including website visits; posts; comments; likes; form submissions; and purchases — that can be tracked; stored; and retrieved

question: In Book 5; students learn RESPONSIBLE USE of the Internet. Which of these is an example of responsible use?

option_c: Using trusted websites; citing sources; avoiding suspicious links; and telling an adult when something online seems wrong
option_d: Opening email attachments from unknown senders

question: What does the HISTORY feature in a web browser show?
option_b: A CHRONOLOGICAL LIST of all websites visited in the current and recent browsing sessions — accessible via Ctrl+H in Edge and Chrome

question: What keyboard shortcut opens BROWSER SETTINGS / HISTORY / DOWNLOADS in Edge?

question: What is a BROWSER EXTENSION (or ADD-ON)?
option_b: A SMALL SOFTWARE PROGRAM that adds extra features or functionality to a web browser — examples: ad blockers; password managers; grammar checkers; screenshot tools

question: What is an AD BLOCKER browser extension?
option_a: A tool that blocks all websites

question: What is the difference between a VIRUS and a WORM in computing?
option_b: A VIRUS attaches to files and requires a USER ACTION to spread (opening a file); a WORM is SELF-REPLICATING and spreads AUTOMATICALLY across networks without user interaction
option_c: A worm is less harmful than a virus
option_d: A virus is worse than a worm

question: What is a TROJAN HORSE in computing?

question: What does 'UPDATE YOUR SOFTWARE' mean and why is it important for security?
option_a: Updates change the look of the software
option_b: SOFTWARE UPDATES patch SECURITY VULNERABILITIES — bugs in old software that hackers can exploit. Keeping operating systems; browsers; and antivirus up to date closes known security holes

question: What is PEER-TO-PEER (P2P) FILE SHARING and what risks does it carry?
option_b: A method of sharing files DIRECTLY BETWEEN USERS over the Internet WITHOUT a central server — carries risks of downloading malware; sharing copyright-protected content illegally; and exposing your device to strangers

question: What does CTRL+L do in a web browser?

question: What is AUTOCOMPLETE in a search engine or browser address bar?

question: What is a "computer network"?
option_b: Two or more computing devices connected together to share resources, data, and services

question: What is a "PAN" (Personal Area Network)?
option_b: A very short-range network (usually up to 10 metres) connecting personal devices around one person — e.g., phone, smartwatch, earbuds via Bluetooth

question: What is a "LAN" (Local Area Network)?
option_b: A network covering a small geographical area — a home, school, or office building — connecting devices within that space

question: What is a "MAN" (Metropolitan Area Network)?
option_b: A network that spans a city or metropolitan area — larger than a LAN but smaller than a WAN

question: What is a "WAN" (Wide Area Network)?
option_b: A network spanning large geographical areas — countries or continents — connecting multiple LANs; the Internet is the largest WAN

question: What is a "client-server" network model?
option_b: A model where client computers request services and a powerful central server provides those services

question: What is a "peer-to-peer" (P2P) network?
option_b: A network where all devices (peers) have equal status and share resources directly with each other without a dedicated server

question: What is a "server" in a network?
option_b: A high-performance computer that provides services (files, printing, email, web) to client computers on the network

question: What is a "network switch"?
option_b: A networking device that connects multiple devices on a LAN and directs data packets only to the specific device they are addressed to

question: What is a "router" in a network?
option_b: A networking device that connects different networks (e.g., a LAN to the Internet) and directs data packets between them

question: What is a "modem"?
option_b: A device that converts digital computer signals to analogue for transmission over phone/cable lines and back again — connecting a LAN to an ISP

question: What is a "wireless access point" (WAP)?
option_b: A networking device that creates a wireless LAN (Wi-Fi) by connecting wirelessly to devices and wired to the network switch

question: What is the "bus topology"?
option_b: All devices connected to a single central cable (the bus); a break in the cable disables the whole network

question: What is the "star topology"?
option_a: All devices linked in a chain
option_b: Each device connects to a central switch or hub; if one connection fails, only that device is affected

question: What is the "ring topology"?
option_b: Each device is connected to exactly two others, forming a closed loop; data travels in one direction around the ring
option_d: Devices connect to a hub only

question: What is the "mesh topology"?
option_b: Every device connects to every other device; highly redundant — data can take many paths

question: What is a "transmission medium"?
option_b: The physical or wireless channel over which data signals travel between network devices — e.g., copper wire, fibre optic cable, or radio waves

question: What is "fibre optic cable"?
option_a: A copper wire with fibre insulation
option_b: A cable that transmits data as pulses of light through glass or plastic fibres — very high speed, long distance, immune to electrical interference

question: What is "twisted-pair cable" (Ethernet cable)?
option_b: Copper cable with pairs of wires twisted together to reduce interference — the most common LAN cable (Cat5e, Cat6)

question: What is "Wi-Fi"?
option_b: A wireless networking technology that allows devices to connect to a LAN using radio waves (IEEE 802.11 standards)

question: What is a "network protocol"?
option_b: A set of rules governing how data is formatted, addressed, transmitted, and received between devices on a network

question: What does "TCP/IP" stand for?
option_b: Transmission Control Protocol / Internet Protocol — the foundational suite governing how data is packaged and routed on the Internet

question: What is an "IP address"?
option_b: A unique numerical label (e.g., 192.168.1.1) assigned to each device on a network to identify it and enable routing

question: What is "bandwidth" in networking?
option_b: The maximum amount of data that can be transmitted over a network connection per unit of time — measured in Mbps or Gbps
option_d: The number of devices on a network

question: What is "latency" in networking?
option_b: The delay between sending a request and receiving a response — measured in milliseconds (ms)

question: What is a "network interface card" (NIC)?
option_b: Hardware built into or added to a device that enables it to connect to a network (wired or wireless)

question: What is a "MAC address"?
option_b: A unique 48-bit hardware identifier permanently assigned to a network interface card by the manufacturer

question: What does a "firewall" do in a network?
option_b: Monitors and filters incoming and outgoing network traffic based on security rules — blocking unauthorised access

question: What is "network security"?
option_b: Protecting a computer network and its data from unauthorised access, misuse, or disruption through hardware, software, and policies

question: What is "data packet" in networking?
option_b: A small unit of data that a message is broken into for transmission across a network, containing the data and addressing information

question: What is an "ISP" (Internet Service Provider)?
option_b: A company that provides customers with access to the Internet — e.g., broadband or mobile data providers

question: What is a "DHCP server"?
option_b: A server that automatically assigns IP addresses to devices joining the network, eliminating manual configuration

question: What is a "DNS server"?
option_b: A server that translates human-readable domain names (www.google.com) into numerical IP addresses that computers can route to

question: What is the advantage of star topology over bus topology?
option_b: If one device's connection fails in star topology only that device loses connection, while in bus a cable fault disables the whole network

question: What does "Ethernet" refer to?
option_b: A family of wired LAN standards defining how data is transmitted over cables (IEEE 802.3) — the most common wired LAN technology

question: What is the purpose of a "hub" vs a "switch"?
option_b: A hub broadcasts data to all connected ports; a switch sends data only to the specific device it is addressed to
option_d: A switch connects to the internet

question: What is a "VPN" (Virtual Private Network)?
option_b: A secure encrypted connection over a public network (Internet) that allows remote users to access a private network as if they were on-site

question: What is a "proxy server"?
option_b: A server that acts as an intermediary between client devices and the Internet — caching content, filtering requests, and providing anonymity

question: What is "encryption" in the context of network security?
option_b: Converting data into an unreadable format (ciphertext) using a key so only authorised parties with the decryption key can read it

question: What is a "network topology"?
option_b: The arrangement (physical or logical) of how nodes and links are structured in a network — e.g., star, bus, ring, mesh

question: What is a "network share" in a client-server network?
option_b: A folder or printer resource made available on a server so authorised users on the network can access it
